title: Solutions to the Einstein-scalar-field system in spherical symmetry with large bounded variation norms
kind: primary paper (arXiv v1 PDF; selective equation and construction audit)
locator: Einstein-scalar normalization and reduced system (1.1)–(1.2), printed pp.1–2; profile definition and outgoing-cone local uniqueness §2.1, printed p.8, equations (2.4)–(2.5); exact Hawking-mass transport equations §2.2, printed pp.8–9, especially (2.10); Theorem 1.7, printed pp.5–6; limiting construction and incoming profile limits §4, printed pp.28–29, especially (4.1); initial Bondi mass definition (1.6), printed p.2. Additional follow-up audit: Proposition 3.3 and Proposition 3.4 (3.16), printed pp.14–17, for uniform decay; §4 estimates immediately preceding (4.1), printed pp.28–29, for uniform lapse and radiation-trace errors; exact fixed-v incoming-mass integration is a deduction from these estimates.
assumptions: For Theorem 1.7: smooth Phi:R→R satisfying (1.7) for some gamma>0, including integral growth bound and sup(|Phi|+|Phi'|)≤epsilon, plus sup|Phi''|<infinity; epsilon sufficiently small depending on gamma, with the note that the limiting construction may require reducing epsilon. Smooth compact profiles satisfy the decay form for any selected 0<gamma<1 after amplitude scaling. System normalization Ric=2 dphi⊗dphi; spherical symmetry; regular axis; double-null gauge lambda=partial_v r; theorem constructs a solution, not a stated unique scattering map.
conclusion: Equation (2.10) gives lambda^{-1}partial_v m=(1/2)(1-mu)r^2(lambda^{-1}partial_v phi)^2. For any global LOY reduced limit with smooth compact Phi, exact flatness before its support sets the incoming integration constant to zero. On each fixed finite v-interval, the source bounds imply r→infinity, phi→0, mu→0, lambda→1/2 and lambda^{-1}partial_v(rphi)→Phi uniformly as u→-infinity. Integrating the exact mass equation from the flat edge yields m_-(V)=(1/4)integral_A^V Phi^2 for each finite V, then E_in=(1/4)integral_R Phi^2. For compact n-dependent smooth parameter families, uniform support, LOY smallness and derivative bounds allow radiation recovery and the mass identity to pass to joint limits. ADM equality remains unproved.
proof_status: Full-text selective audit of exact normalization, mass transport equation, Theorem 1.7 hypotheses, global limiting construction, uniform decay and section 4 lapse/radiation estimates. Independently integrated the transport equation on a fixed finite v-interval of the global limit; this establishes actual incoming boundary mass without differentiating a limit or interchanging a moving cone vertex. Also audited uniformity needed for a compact finite-dimensional n-dependent profile family. Finite-cone continuity and parameter-uniform readout compactness for the proposed degree theorem remain separate gates.
dependencies: Theorem 1.7 uses estimates for finite outgoing-cone data uniform in u0, takes u0→−infinity, and proves causal geodesic completeness in §6. Local characteristic uniqueness §2.1 is for finite-cone data. A uniqueness theorem for the selected limiting solution from past-null-infinity profiles is not asserted in Theorem 1.7.
limits: This establishes the iterated incoming boundary mass for compact profiles in the LOY reduced global solution category. It does not establish the spatial diagonal ADM limit or its equality with incoming mass, nor smooth four-dimensional axis reconstruction. Theorem 1.7 does not state uniqueness of the global limit; existential degree arguments may use target-specific subsequences if finite-cone continuity and joint compactness/readout passage are proved.
open_questions: Can the spatial diagonal ADM limit and its equality with the iterated incoming boundary mass be proved for this family? Do the proposed finite-cone readout maps have the required continuity and uniform remainder, and can the n-dependent compactness passage be completed through the central clocks and readings?
relevance: Primary source for the exact nonlinear Hawking-mass flux in the Ric=2 dphi⊗dphi normalization and for the compact-profile past-null-infinity scattering construction. Direct finite-cone integration fixes the incoming energy coefficient at 1/4 for Phi=2∂v(rphi); later-pulse energy compensation follows from disjoint profile supports, subject to exact pre-tail solution matching.
